label: Figure 1
title: GLAST-positive extracellular vesicles define a glial-enriched paired-RNA compartment
explanation: Orthogonal physical, imaging, protein and RNA measurements establish a rare GLAST-positive vesicle fraction that supports matched miRNA and mRNA profiling before feature selection.

label: Figure 2
title: A low-variance paired-RNA program tracks ALS survival through directional states
explanation: Outcome-guided MOFA identifies a low-variance factor shared across the two RNA layers. Candidate selection and directional miRNA–mRNA pairing connect this factor to survival.

label: Figure 3
title: The five-miRNA program transfers to total plasma and adds later-horizon prognostic information
explanation: Five directionally concordant miRNAs transfer from GLAST-positive vesicles to total plasma and add information to ALSFRS-R slope and NfL, particularly at later prediction horizons.

label: Figure 4
title: A circulating EV-derived mRNA score tracks reactive glial and vascular states in human ALS cortex
explanation: The fixed EV-derived mRNA candidates map into independent cortical datasets and identify a five-gene bridge associated with reactive astrocytic, vascular and oligodendroglial states.

label: Figure 5
title: Circulating RNA arms converge on a cortical neuroimmune–neurovascular program
explanation: Target, pathway and lineage evidence place the selected miRNA and mRNA arms in an inflammatory and vascular program opposed to myelin and axon–glia support.

label: Extended Data Figure 1
title: Complementary characterization of the GLAST-positive vesicle fraction
explanation: Nano-flow cytometry and dSTORM show a heterogeneous tetraspanin phenotype and platform-dependent particle-size estimates, supporting a GLAST-enriched rather than uniformly canonical vesicle population.

label: Extended Data Figure 2
title: EV-RNA composition is related to age sex sequencing depth and clinical variables
explanation: Global cargo composition varies more strongly with demographic and sequencing-depth measures than with diagnosis, motivating depth-aware sensitivity analyses.

label: Extended Data Figure 3
title: Sequence architecture maps candidate EV-RNA sorting and RBP motifs
explanation: The recovered RNA contains prespecified miRNA EXOmotifs and mRNA 3′-UTR or RNA-binding-protein motifs, but motif prevalence does not differ after multiple-testing correction.

label: Extended Data Figure 4
title: Recurrent non-canonical junctions form a sparse sample-specific landscape
explanation: Recurrent junction recovery is sparse and strongly depth dependent. The absence of canonical TDP-43-associated cryptic junctions is therefore interpreted as coverage limited.

label: Extended Data Figure 5
title: Factor 1 loadings disease effects and clinical context
explanation: Candidate features are supported by intersecting Factor 1 loading, disease abundance and survival evidence rather than by any single statistical contrast.

label: Extended Data Figure 6
title: Directional pair states link the paired-RNA program to survival
explanation: Prior-supported miRNA–mRNA links shift toward the suppression state in shorter survival, whereas same-direction states provide an internal negative control.

label: Extended Data Figure 7
title: EV-anchored miRNAs retain measurable signal in total plasma
explanation: The EV-nominated miRNAs remain measurable in plasma, while depth, longitudinal stability and outcome-aligned processing batch define important technical boundaries.

label: Extended Data Figure 8
title: Plasma-five performance across horizons classifiers and clinical baselines
explanation: The broad horizon-dependent performance ordering is retained across seven classifier families and clinical baselines, while absolute calibration remains exploratory.

label: Extended Data Figure 9
title: Independent cortical datasets establish cross-disease context
explanation: Bulk and donor-pseudobulk cortical analyses show that the fixed five-mRNA panel retains discriminatory information across regions and disease comparators.

label: Extended Data Figure 10
title: Lineage gating resolves cargo-state associations
explanation: Lineage gating separates identity programs from shared responses and shows significant gene–program associations without including cargo genes in the state-program definitions.
